results.sentence2: The EPS security context most recently used by the network is called current. It can be native or mapped. The KSI is assigned by MME during authentication or inter-system handover.

results.sentence1: The UE shall use its current EPS security context to protect TAU or Attach requests. If MME receives a request with a non-current context, it becomes current and overwrites the existing one.
results.sentence2: The KSI indicates whether the EPS security context is native or mapped. When native, KSI = KSIASME; when mapped, KSI = KSISGSN. EPS security context indicated by KSI can be reused without new authentication.

results.sentence1: The UE shall use its current EPS security context to protect TAU or Attach requests. If MME receives a request with a non-current context, it becomes current and overwrites the existing one.
results.sentence2: The EPS security context associated with the KSI is no longer valid. UE and MME may maintain both current and non-current contexts after re-authentication.

results.sentence1: The UE shall use its current EPS security context to protect TAU or Attach requests. If MME receives a request with a non-current context, it becomes current and overwrites the existing one.
results.sentence2: The security mode command includes the KSI of the new EPS security context. It is integrity protected but not ciphered. UE responds with a message protected and ciphered with the new context.

results.sentence1: The UE shall use its current EPS security context to protect TAU or Attach requests. If MME receives a request with a non-current context, it becomes current and overwrites the existing one.
results.sentence2: If the current context is native, it becomes non-current native and overwrites existing non-current native. The network replaces a mapped EPS context after CS to PS handover.

results.sentence1: UE uses its current EPS security context to protect TAU/Attach. If MME receives a request with a non-current context, it becomes current and overwrites the existing one.
results.sentence2: If current EPS context is native, it becomes non-current native and overwrites existing non-current native. If CS to PS handover fails, delete the new mapped EPS security context.

results.sentence1: UE uses its current EPS security context to protect TAU/Attach. If MME receives a request with a non-current context, it becomes current and overwrites the existing one.
results.sentence2: If UE has a mapped EPS context, it sets the security context flag to "mapped". Otherwise, it sets it to "native". If UE has a valid GUTI, it populates the EPS mobile identity.

results.sentence1: UE uses its current EPS security context to protect TAU/Attach. If MME receives a request with a non-current context, it becomes current and overwrites the existing one.
results.sentence2: Network starts timer T3422. If detach type indicates re-attach and cause is not IMSI unknown, MME either stores current native EPS context or deletes mapped EPS context.

results.sentence1: UE's replayed security capabilities include NR capabilities if MME supports them. If NAS security mode command is sent after an attach/TAU request without integrity protection, MME calculates a hash and includes it in the command.
results.sentence2: After receiving an attach or TAU request without integrity, MME calculates hash of the message and includes it in the security mode command as per 3GPP 33.401. MME may also request IMEISV.

results.sentence1: NAS security mode reject and all following NAS messages are protected with the old EPS security context until a new one is established.
results.sentence2: Security mode command includes KSI of new EPS context. It is integrity protected but not ciphered. UE responds with message integrity protected and ciphered with new context. MME can also modify or activate contexts.

results.sentence1: NAS security mode reject and all following NAS messages are protected with the old EPS security context until a new one is established.
results.sentence2: MME re-derives NAS keys with new algorithm identities and includes them in the security mode command. The message is integrity protected with the new EPS context during attach/TAU.

results.sentence1: NAS security mode reject and all following NAS messages are protected with the old EPS security context until a new one is established.
results.sentence2: UE resets uplink NAS count when taking a new EPS security context into use after authentication. The command includes type flag set to "mapped" and integrity check passes before use.

results.sentence1: If no EPS NAS security context existed, NAS security mode reject cannot be protected. If NAS count wrap occurs, UE releases NAS connection instead of sending the reject.
results.sentence2: UE resets uplink NAS count when taking a new EPS security context into use after authentication. The command includes type flag set to "mapped" and integrity check passes before use.

results.sentence1: If UE and MME have a non-current native and a current mapped EPS context, they make the non-current native current and delete mapped or partial contexts.
results.sentence2: The most recently used EPS context is called current, and it can be native or mapped. KSI is assigned during EPS authentication or inter-system handover.

results.sentence1: If UE and MME have a non-current native and a current mapped EPS context, they make the non-current native current and delete mapped or partial contexts.
results.sentence2: After inter-system handover, UE and MME can have both a mapped EPS context as current and a non-current native EPS context. After successful EPS re-authentication, delete non-current contexts.

results.sentence1: If UE and MME have a non-current native and a current mapped EPS context, they make the non-current native current and delete mapped or partial contexts.
results.sentence2: Previously current native becomes non-current. If new mapped context is created during inter-system handover, delete existing mapped. When taking a non-current native into use, delete current mapped.

results.sentence1: If UE and MME have a non-current native and a current mapped EPS context, they make the non-current native current and delete mapped or partial contexts.
results.sentence2: If current EPS context is native and handover fails, delete derived mapped EPS context for PS domain.

results.sentence1: After AKA, derive new NAS keys from new KASME or activate native security context with low NAS count before wraparound.
results.sentence2: If NAS count close to wrap, initiate new AKA or use non-current native EPS context with low NAS count; reset counters when activated.

results.sentence1: Once NAS integrity is active, messages without integrity protection are rejected. Before that, unprotected NAS messages are accepted only in certain cases.
results.sentence2: Security header rules apply regardless of algorithm used. If null integrity is selected, messages with integrity header are treated as protected.

results.sentence1: UE uses uplink NAS count for NAS-token calculation and increments stored count.
results.sentence2: Receiver estimates sender NAS count, increments overflow on wrap, ensures each count accepted once. During inter-system change, UE increments uplink NAS count after NAS token derivation.

results.sentence1: If MME finds a match, it sets stored uplink NAS count as if an integrity-protected NAS message was received.
results.sentence2: Each EPS context has two NAS count counters (uplink and downlink), 24-bit internally, forming a 32-bit value for security algorithms.

results.sentence1: MME selects highest-priority NAS algorithms from its list and UE capabilities, derives NAS keys from K'ASME, and includes details in handover request.
results.sentence2: MME includes selected NAS algorithms, nonceMME, and KSI in NAS security container for E-UTRAN handover; UE derives K'ASME using nonceMME.

results.sentence1: Uplink and downlink NAS counts for mapped EPS context are set to zero; mapped EPS context becomes current.
results.sentence2: Current EPS context is the one most recently used by the network, which can be native or mapped and is identified by KSI.

results.sentence1: Uplink and downlink NAS counts for mapped EPS context are set to zero; mapped EPS context becomes current.
results.sentence2: MME stores mapped EPS NAS context with counters tied to derived K'ASME; re-establishes secure NAS exchange with tracking area update accept.

results.sentence1: Uplink and downlink NAS counts for mapped EPS context are set to zero; mapped EPS context becomes current.
results.sentence2: MME stores mapped EPS NAS context with counters tied to derived K'ASME; re-establishes secure NAS exchange with attach accept.

results.sentence1: Uplink and downlink NAS count values for the mapped EPS security context shall be reset to 0; mapped EPS context becomes current.
results.sentence2: ME applies derived NAS keys, resets NAS counters to 0, and replaces existing mapped EPS context after CS to PS handover completes.

results.sentence1: Uplink and downlink NAS count values for the mapped EPS security context shall be reset to 0; mapped EPS context becomes current.
results.sentence2: UE resets uplink NAS count when receiving security mode command for a new EPS context after successful authentication; message includes type flag and KSI.

results.sentence1: EPS security context at AS and NAS level overwrites current mapped context. If current context is native, it becomes non-current. Handover failure makes new mapped context unusable.
results.sentence2: Current EPS security context is the one most recently used by the network; it can be native or mapped, identified by KSI assigned during authentication or inter-system handover.

results.sentence1: EPS security context at AS and NAS level overwrites current mapped context. If current context is native, it becomes non-current. Handover failure makes new mapped context unusable.
results.sentence2: KSI indicates whether an EPS context is native or mapped. Native contexts use KSiasme, mapped use KSisgsn; contexts can be reused without new authentication.

results.sentence1: EPS security context at AS and NAS level overwrites current mapped context. If current context is native, it becomes non-current. Handover failure makes new mapped context unusable.
results.sentence2: If a new mapped context is derived during inter-system handover, old mapped context is deleted. Previously current native context becomes non-current; partial contexts are removed.

results.sentence1: EPS security context at AS and NAS level overwrites current mapped context. If current context is native, it becomes non-current. If handover fails, new mapped context can't be used.
results.sentence2: Security mode command message includes KSI of new EPS context. MME sends it integrity-protected, UE replies encrypted. MME may modify or switch EPS contexts using this command.

results.sentence1: EPS security context at AS and NAS level overwrites current mapped context. If current context is native, it becomes non-current. If handover fails, new mapped context can't be used.
results.sentence2: If current EPS context is native, it becomes non-current and overwrites any old native context in ME. Network replaces mapped EPS context after successful CS to PS handover.

results.sentence1: EPS security context at AS and NAS level overwrites current mapped context. If current context is native, it becomes non-current. If handover fails, new mapped context can't be used.
results.sentence2: If current EPS context is native, it becomes non-current and overwrites old native context in MME. If CS to PS handover fails, UE and network delete new mapped EPS context.

results.sentence1: UE includes KSiasme in TAU request only if it has native EPS context. MME deletes or reuses native EPS contexts based on TAU request content and GUTI.
results.sentence2: Previously current native EPS context becomes non-current; partial contexts may be deleted. When mapped context is created during handover, old mapped context is removed.

results.sentence1: UE includes KSiasme in TAU request only if it has native EPS context. MME deletes or reuses native EPS contexts based on TAU request content and GUTI.
results.sentence2: UE resets NAS counters when mapped EPS context is activated. If UE has non-current native context, it includes KSiasme and GUTI in the TAU or tracking area update message.

results.sentence1: UE includes KSiasme in TAU request only if it has native EPS security context. If MME receives TAU request with KSiasme and GUTI matching stored non-current native context, it knows UE and MME share that context. If request lacks KSiasme, MME deletes any stored non-current native context for this UE.
results.sentence2: If UE holds a valid GUTI, it indicates it in the additional GUTI IE. If UE has non-current native EPS context, it includes KSiasme in the tracking area update request message.

results.sentence1: UE includes KSiasme in TAU request only if it has native EPS security context. If MME receives TAU request with KSiasme and GUTI matching stored non-current native context, it knows UE and MME share that context. If request lacks KSiasme, MME deletes any stored non-current native context for this UE.
results.sentence2: MME verifies UE security capabilities in TAU request. If the request does not contain a valid KSiasme in the non-current native NAS key identifier IE, MME deletes the non-current native EPS context for this UE.

results.sentence1: UE includes KSiasme in TAU request only if it has native EPS security context. If MME receives TAU request with KSiasme and GUTI matching stored non-current native context, it knows UE and MME share that context. If request lacks KSiasme, MME deletes any stored non-current native context for this UE.
results.sentence2: MME verifies UE security capabilities in TAU request. If request lacks valid KSiasme, MME deletes non-current native EPS context for this UE.

results.sentence1: MME discards any CK, IK, KC, CKsn, and KSI from old SGSN during context request and creates mapped EPS security context by setting K'ASME = CK'PS || IK'PS received from CS-to-PS handover request.
results.sentence2: MSC associates CK'PS and IK'PS with a KSI'PS, then transfers CK'PS, IK'PS, and KSI'PS to MME.

results.sentence1: MME discards any CK, IK, KC, CKsn, and KSI from old SGSN during context request and creates mapped EPS security context by setting K'ASME = CK'PS || IK'PS received from CS-to-PS handover request.
results.sentence2: MME creates mapped EPS security context by setting K'ASME to CK'PS || IK'PS received from MSC and associates it with KSI S-GSN.

results.sentence1: MME associates K'ASME with KSI S-GSN. The KSI S-GSN value matches the KSI'PS received in the CS-to-PS handover request.
results.sentence2: The ME associates K'ASME with KSI S-GSN. The ME sets KSI S-GSN to the value received in the NAS security transparent container from the network.

results.sentence1: Using mapped key K'ASME and initial uplink NAS count value of 2^32-1. Uplink and downlink NAS count values for the mapped EPS security context start at 0. If MME lacks UE EPS security capabilities, it assumes the default set of EPS security algorithms and sets them in the mapped context.
results.sentence2: MME stores mapped EPS NAS security context with uplink and downlink NAS count counters initialized and re-establishes NAS security by sending a TAU Accept message integrity-protected and ciphered with the mapped context.

results.sentence1: Using mapped key K'ASME and initial uplink NAS count value of 2^32-1. Uplink and downlink NAS count values for the mapped EPS security context start at 0. If MME lacks UE EPS security capabilities, it assumes the default set of EPS security algorithms and sets them in the mapped context.
results.sentence2: MME stores mapped EPS NAS security context with uplink and downlink counters initialized and re-establishes NAS security by sending an Attach Accept message integrity-protected and ciphered with the mapped context.

results.sentence1: MME overwrites any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: The EPS security context most recently used by the network is called the current EPS security context. It can be native or mapped, and its EKSI is assigned by the MME during EPS authentication or inter-system handover.

results.sentence1: MME overwrites any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: EKSI consists of a value and a security context type (native or mapped). Native contexts use KSiasme; mapped contexts use KSisgsn. The context identified by an EKSI can be reused for NAS security without a new EPS authentication or by triggering a security mode control procedure.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: After inter-system handover, UE and MME may hold a mapped EPS security context (current) and a non-current native EPS security context from previous S1 access. After EPS re-authentication, any non-current EPS security context is deleted. When a partial native EPS security context is activated, the previous current context is deleted.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: The previously current native EPS security context becomes non-current, and any partial native context is deleted unless none exists. When a new mapped EPS security context is derived during inter-system handover, the previous mapped context is deleted. When a full non-current native EPS security context is activated, the previous mapped context is deleted.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current and overwrites any existing non-current native context. Network replaces mapped EPS security context only after successful CS to PS SRVCC handover.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current and overwrites any existing non-current native context. If CS to PS SRVCC handover fails, the derived mapped EPS security context is deleted.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: When UE has or is establishing a PDN connection for emergency services or is attaching for RLOS, the UE does not regenerate KASME. The security mode command is used to derive and activate a native EPS security context with KSI=000 and null algorithms allowed only in these emergency scenarios.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: If the UE has a mapped EPS security context as current, it sets the type of security context flag to "mapped"; otherwise, it sets it to "native." If UE has a valid GUTI, it populates the EPS mobile identity IE with the valid GUTI.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing current mapped EPS security context with the newly created one. If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current.
results.sentence2: The network starts timer T3422. Depending on detach type and EMM cause, the MME either stores the current EPS security context if native or deletes it if mapped.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing non-current EPS security context with this current native EPS security context. CS to PS HO confirmation and following AS messages in E-UTRAN shall be ciphered and integrity protected. If SRVCC handover fails, the new mapped EPS security context cannot be used in the future.
results.sentence2: If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current and overwrites any existing non-current native EPS security context. The network replaces an already established mapped EPS security context after successful CS to PS SRVCC handover.

results.sentence1: MME and ME overwrite any existing non-current EPS security context with this current native EPS security context. CS to PS HO confirmation and following AS messages in E-UTRAN shall be ciphered and integrity protected. If SRVCC handover fails, the new mapped EPS security context cannot be used in the future.
results.sentence2: If the current EPS security context is native, it becomes non-current and overwrites any existing non-current native EPS security context. If CS to PS SRVCC handover fails, the UE and network delete the derived mapped EPS security context.

results.sentence1: If EIA0 is used for NAS integrity protection, it will always be used for AS. If the UE initiates an RLOS connection, it may accept EIA0 for NAS and RRC signaling protection. The UE shall support mitigations in J.1.3 to reduce lack of network authentication for RLOS. UE in LSM wishing to initiate RLOS must perform checks before starting attach, including enforcing access control on apps authorized to initiate RLOS.
results.sentence2: The UE shall not attempt to request RLOS if PLMN does not support it. Only authorized applications may trigger RLOS initiation. For UE attached for RLOS, only UE-originated requests are supported.
